skins.title: Lunch break
skins.situation: You and Meera take lunch at the same time. Each of you heads either to the canteen or to the dhaba across the road. Your phones are out of charge. The canteen cook serves whoever comes.

incentives.m1.s.meet: You like the canteen more; Meera likes the dhaba more. Each of you would rather eat together than alone, and eating alone is worse at the other person’s favourite place.

skins.timing: You both set off at the same time. Neither of you sees where the other goes.
skins.information: You both know what the other likes. You don’t know where Meera will go.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your place and Meera’s place

skins.title: The team update
skins.situation: You and Ravi each start this week’s team update, either as a document or as slides. Your manager, Ms Iyer, reads whatever arrives on Friday.

incentives.m1.s.meet: You work faster in a document; Ravi works faster in slides. You would both rather use one format than two, and two formats are worse when each of you uses the other’s favourite.

skins.timing: You both start on the same morning. Neither sees the other’s draft until it is done.
skins.information: You both know how the other likes to work. You don’t know which format Ravi will pick.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your format and Ravi’s format

skins.title: Weekend training
skins.situation: You and Kabir both want to train at the club this weekend, at the morning session or the evening session. Coach Sharma runs both sessions either way.

incentives.m1.s.meet: You like mornings more; Kabir likes evenings more. Each of you would rather train together than alone, and training alone is worse at the time the other likes.

skins.timing: You each sign up at the same time. Neither sees the other’s sign-up.
skins.information: You both know which time the other likes. You don’t know which session Kabir will pick.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your session and Kabir’s session

skins.title: The craft stall
skins.situation: You and Tara sell handmade crafts and share one van. This weekend each of you books a stall at either the town mela or the riverside market. The organisers rent stalls to anyone.

incentives.m1.s.meet: You sell more at the town mela; Tara sells more by the river. Sharing the van to one place beats going to two, and going alone is worse at the other’s favourite place.

skins.timing: You both book at the same time. Neither sees the other’s booking.
skins.information: You both know where the other sells best. You don’t know where Tara will book.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your market and Tara’s market

skins.title: The park clean-up
skins.situation: Your housing society is planning a park clean-up. You fix the date first: a weekday or the weekend. Asha, who leads a volunteer group, reads your notice and then decides whether her group joins yours or holds its own event later.

incentives.m1.s.turns: You can lead only on a weekday, and either way you want Asha’s group to join. Her group is free at weekends: on a weekend date they want to join; on a weekday they would rather hold their own event.

skins.timing: You choose first. Asha chooses after reading your notice.
skins.information: Asha sees your date before deciding. You know what Asha’s group wants.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your date and Asha’s reply

skins.title: Token and dial
skins.situation: A two-step puzzle. You move a token first, left or right. The other side sees your move, then turns a dial up or down.

incentives.m1.s.turns: You score a bonus for moving the token left, and a smaller one if the dial ends up. The other side wants the dial down after left and up after right, and likes right-then-up best.

skins.timing: You move first. The other side moves after seeing yours.
skins.information: The other side sees your move before choosing. Each side knows what the other wants.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your move and the dial

skins.title: Cooking dinner
skins.situation: You are cooking dinner. You decide first whether to make rice or rotis. Your brother Sahil sees what you started and then makes dal or a curry to go with it.

incentives.m1.s.turns: Rice is much quicker for you to make, and you also like dal more than curry. Sahil likes curry with rice but dal with rotis, and rotis with dal is his favourite meal.

skins.timing: You choose first. Sahil chooses after seeing what you are making.
skins.information: Sahil knows what you started before choosing. You both know each other’s tastes.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your dish and Sahil’s side dish

skins.title: The delivery van
skins.situation: You run a small online shop. You first book the early van or the late van for today’s orders. Lina at the warehouse sees your booking and then decides whether to help load it or work through her own list.

incentives.m1.s.turns: The early van costs you much less, and you would also like Lina’s help. Lina is free in the evening: she would help with the late van but keep to her own list for the early one.

skins.timing: You book first. Lina decides after seeing which van you booked.
skins.information: Lina knows your booking before choosing. You know her timetable.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your van and Lina’s choice

skins.title: Planning Sunday
skins.situation: You and Nikhil are planning Sunday. At the same moment, you post the place, the museum or the lake, and Nikhil posts the start time: morning, noon or evening. His sister Pooja will drive you both, wherever and whenever.

incentives.m1.s.three: You most want the museum in the morning, and how the day goes for you depends on the time Nikhil picks. Nikhil most wants the museum at noon.

skins.timing: You both post at the same moment. Neither sees the other’s post first.
skins.information: You know what Nikhil likes. You don’t know which time he will post.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your place and Nikhil’s start time

skins.title: The reading circle
skins.situation: Your reading circle meets this week. You choose whether it meets in person or online. At the same time Zoya chooses what to read: a short story, a novel or a play. Mr Das, who owns the café, hosts whatever is chosen.

incentives.m1.s.three: You enjoy meeting in person most when the reading is a short story, and how the evening goes for you depends on what Zoya picks. Zoya enjoys a novel in person most.

skins.timing: You and Zoya decide at the same time. Neither sees the other’s choice first.
skins.information: You know what Zoya enjoys. You don’t know what she will pick.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your format and Zoya’s reading

skins.title: Two tiffin services
skins.situation: You and Hari run tiffin services in the same lane. Today you set your price, regular or discount, while Hari sets his menu: simple, mixed or special. One delivery rider carries both services’ boxes.

incentives.m1.s.three: You earn most at your regular price when Hari offers the simple menu, and how your day goes depends on his menu. Hari earns most when you keep the regular price and he offers mixed.

skins.timing: You both decide in the morning at the same time. Neither knows the other’s choice until lunch.
skins.information: You know how Hari’s customers think. You don’t know which menu he will offer.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your price and Hari’s menu

skins.title: A friendly match
skins.situation: In a friendly cricket match you captain the fielding side and set an attacking or a defensive field. At the same time Jaya, the batting captain, sets her order: aggressive, steady or cautious. The umpire runs the game whatever you both choose.

incentives.m1.s.three: You do best with an attacking field against an aggressive order, and your result depends on Jaya’s order. Jaya does best with a steady order against an attacking field.

skins.timing: Both of you decide before the first ball. Neither sees the other’s plan.
skins.information: You know how Jaya likes to bat. You don’t know which order she will choose.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your field and Jaya’s batting order

skins.title: Library volunteers
skins.situation: You and Kiran volunteer at the community library. This Saturday each of you signs up for one shift, opening or closing. Mrs Pillai, the librarian, keeps the doors open all day regardless.

incentives.m1.s.meet: You like the opening shift more; Kiran likes closing more. Both of you enjoy a shared shift more than a lone one, and a lone shift is worse when it is the one the other likes.

skins.timing: You sign up at the same time. Neither sees the other’s name on the sheet.
skins.information: You know which shift Kiran likes. You don’t know which one Kiran will take.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your shift and Kiran’s shift

skins.title: The book stall
skins.situation: At your second-hand book stall you name your asking price first, high or low. Anil, a regular buyer, hears your price and then decides to buy now or wait until next week.

incentives.m1.s.turns: A high price earns you much more on each book, and you would also like Anil to buy now. Anil would wait at a high price but buy now at a low price, which suits him best.

skins.timing: You name a price first. Anil decides after hearing it.
skins.information: Anil hears your price before deciding. You know how he shops.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your price and Anil’s reply

skins.title: The morning trek
skins.situation: You and Rohan plan to walk together on Sunday. You set off first, by the north gate or the lake path. Rohan leaves an hour later and must pick a route too. There is no phone signal on the hill.

incentives.m1.s.unseen: You like the north gate route most, and the walk is better with Rohan along. Walking alone, you still prefer the north gate. Rohan just wants to walk with you; either route suits him equally.

skins.timing: You leave first. Rohan leaves later, without knowing which route you took.
skins.information: Rohan cannot see or ask which way you went. You both know what the other likes.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your route and Rohan’s route

skins.title: The site visit
skins.situation: You and Farid must sign off a delivery together today at one of two building sites. You drive out first, to the east site or the west site. Farid leaves the office later. The site phones are down all day.

incentives.m1.s.unseen: The east site is nearer your next meeting, and signing off together saves you a second trip. Alone, you still prefer the east site. Farid wants to be where you are; either site suits him.

skins.timing: You leave first. Farid chooses his site later, without hearing from you.
skins.information: Farid cannot find out which site you chose. You both know what the other wants.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your site and Farid’s site

skins.title: The family outing
skins.situation: You and your cousin Meenal want to spend Saturday afternoon together in town. You head out first, to the old market or the riverside. Meenal finishes work later and then heads to one of them. Her phone is being repaired.

incentives.m1.s.unseen: You enjoy the old market most, and the afternoon is better with Meenal there. On your own, you still prefer the market. Meenal only cares about finding you; the two places are equal for her.

skins.timing: You go first. Meenal goes later, without word from you.
skins.information: Meenal cannot learn where you went. You both know what the other enjoys.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your place and Meenal’s place

skins.title: Two covered boxes
skins.situation: You put a token in the left box or the right box, and the box is covered at once. Later the other side puts a token in one of the two boxes without lifting any cover.

incentives.m1.s.unseen: You score most with both tokens in the left box, then both in the right; apart, left beats right for you. The other side scores the same for either match and wants the tokens together.

skins.timing: You place first. The other side places later, with every box covered.
skins.information: The other side cannot see where your token is. Each side knows the rules.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your box and the other side’s box

skins.title: Meeting after class
skins.situation: You and your friend Sneha want to meet after your evening class. Your class ends first, so you walk to the corner café or the book café. Sneha’s class ends later; then she picks one. Your phone battery is dead.

incentives.m1.s.unseen: You prefer the corner café, and an evening with Sneha is better than one alone. Alone, you still prefer the corner café. Sneha just wants to find you; both cafés are the same to her.

skins.timing: You arrive first. Sneha chooses later, without a message from you.
skins.information: Sneha has no way to know which café you picked. You both know what the other wants.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your café and Sneha’s café

skins.title: Switch and three dials
skins.situation: A test rig has your switch and the other side’s dial. You flip the switch up or down. At the same moment, the other side sets its dial to low, mid or high, without seeing your switch.

incentives.m1.s.three: You score highest switching up when the dial reads low, and how the reading comes out for you depends on the dial. The other side scores highest when you switch up and it sets the dial to mid.

skins.timing: You both choose at the same moment: switch and dial move together. Neither of you sees the other’s setting first.
skins.information: You know how the other side’s scoring works. You don’t know which dial setting it will choose.
skins.matrixLabel: Outcomes for your switch and the other side’s dial

rubrics.prompt: Describe this situation in your own words: who decides, what each can choose, who knows what, and what each wants.

criteria.text: Names everyone whose choice changes the result, and nobody else.
criteria.meets: “Meera and I each pick where to eat.”
criteria.misses: “The cook, Meera and I are all involved.”

criteria.text: Lists the options open to each person.
criteria.meets: “Each of us can go to the canteen or the dhaba.”

criteria.text: Says who knows what, and whether anyone sees the other’s choice first.
criteria.meets: “We choose at the same time without seeing each other.”

criteria.text: States what each person wants, including how the other’s choice matters to them.
criteria.meets: “I like the canteen more, but we both want to eat together.”
